questions.q: What are the four defining characteristics (the "4 C's") of every Oracle Fusion ledger?
options: Chart of accounts, calendar, currency, and accounting method
Cost center, customer, credit, and collections
Code, class, category, and class type
Company, country, currency, calendar
questions.explain: Every ledger is defined by its chart of accounts, calendar, currency, and subledger accounting method.

questions.q: How many primary ledgers does an accounting configuration require?
options: Zero — primary ledgers are optional
Exactly one, mandatory primary ledger
At least three, one per subledger
As many as there are legal entities
questions.explain: Every accounting configuration is built around exactly one mandatory primary ledger.

questions.q: What is a secondary ledger used for?
options: It only ever changes the currency, never the chart of accounts
It replaces the primary ledger entirely
It maintains an optional, alternative accounting representation of the same business activity, tied to a primary ledger
It is required before any legal entity can be registered
questions.explain: A secondary ledger is optional and associated with a primary ledger, and can differ in chart of accounts, calendar, currency, or accounting method to provide an alternate accounting view.

questions.q: How does a reporting currency differ from a secondary ledger?
options: A reporting currency is mandatory for every accounting configuration
A reporting currency always requires its own legal entity
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
A reporting currency restates the same ledger's data in another currency, rather than providing a different accounting method or chart of accounts
questions.explain: A reporting currency is just the same primary or secondary ledger's data translated into another currency — "the same book, translated" — not an alternate accounting representation.

questions.q: If two ledgers share identical chart of accounts and calendar/period type, what later concept becomes possible for them?
options: They automatically merge into one legal entity
They become candidates for a ledger set
They can no longer be used for subledger accounting
They must be converted into business units
questions.explain: Ledgers that share the same chart of accounts and calendar/period type combination can be grouped into a ledger set, covered in the next lesson.
